display.title: Episode 239: The Stargazer
display.summary_short: As summer ends, Uncle Yossi asks children to share how they brought friends closer to Yiddishkeit; then a stargazer predicts a young man's death, and a piece of bread given to a beggar changes everything.
display.summary_long: Broadcast as summer vacation 5746 was winding down. Uncle Yossi explains that summer is a time to strengthen body and soul, and that a Tzivos Hashem soldier helps new friends learn about yeshiva, brachos and the Shema; he invites listeners to write in with stories of how they did so. After the Hakochainik march, he introduces the special power of tzedakah, which can add years to a person's life, and two boys lead the Shema. Story time: a stargazer in the marketplace, mocked by the crowd, predicts that a young man walking into the forest will not come back alive. The young man returns cheerful, and when questioned he recalls giving bread to a starving old man, at which moment a snake slipped out of his sack. The stargazer concludes that the gift of charity overruled the stars, as Shlomo HaMelech wrote: tzedakah saves from death. Uncle Yossi then reminds listeners to say the Twelve Pesukim daily, plays a short family scene and song about 'Torah tziva lanu Moshe', and closes with a talk about Shabbos and this Friday's candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Tzedakah saves from death and brings Hashem's blessings; give some every day.
